# feris.ir — source

Static site, built by `build.py` (Python stdlib only, no dependencies to install).

## Layout

```
content/en/site.md        Resume content (English)
content/fa/site.md        Resume content (Persian)
content/en/blog/*.md      Blog posts (English)
content/fa/blog/*.md      Blog posts (Persian)
build.py                  Generates everything below from the above
assets/farzad.png         Shared photo

# generated by build.py — do not edit directly, edit content/ instead
index.html                Root: redirects by browser language
en/, fa/                  Resume + blog, one tree per language
sitemap.xml
```

## Adding a blog post

1. Create `content/<lang>/blog/<slug>.md` (`<lang>` is `en` or `fa`; write both if you want the post bilingual — they don't have to match 1:1).
2. Frontmatter at the top:
   ```
   ---
   title: Post title
   date: 2026-09-19
   excerpt: One or two sentences shown on the blog index and used as the meta description.
   ---
   ```
3. Body in plain Markdown: paragraphs, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `# / ## / ###` headings, `- ` bullet lists, `1. ` numbered lists, and `[text](url)` links.
4. Run:
   ```
   python3 build.py
   ```
5. Commit and push. The filename (without `.md`) becomes the post's URL: `content/en/blog/my-post.md` → `/en/blog/my-post/`.

## Editing the resume

Edit `content/en/site.md` or `content/fa/site.md` directly (same format: `## section` headers, `### Sub | header | pieces` for repeated items like jobs), then `python3 build.py` and push.

## Notes

- `.nojekyll` keeps GitHub Pages from running Jekyll over these files (Jekyll would try to process the blog posts' frontmatter as its own pages).
- The Person JSON-LD schema on each resume page is generated automatically from `site.md` at build time — no manual sync needed.
- `robots.txt` disallows `/content/` since it's the raw source, not meant to be indexed.
